newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 10.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
BIHAR CHIEF MINISTER GOES ON THE OFFENSIVE

Bihar chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav said he would not quit either the post of chief minister or that of the Janata Dal (JD) president even if he was charged in the animal husbandry case. This was even as his supporters disrupted air and rail traffic in Patna. They were protesting against Central Bureau of Investment joint director U.N. Biswas' statement indicating that Yadav would shortly be charged. Meanwhile, United Front sources, both within the JD and other constituents, said the question of what to do in Bihar would arise only if and when the chief minister was actually charged.
Indian Express
FORMER CONGRESS STALWARTS BACK IN PARENT PARTY

Congress president Sitaram Kesri readmitted All India Indira Congress leaders N.D. Tiwari and Arjun Singh to the Congress. The Congress president's decision came after he established complete control over the organisation by winning the leadership of the Congress Parliamentary Party. The position of two ministers from the Tiwari camp in the United Front government - Satpal Maharaj and Sis Ram Ola - however, remained unchanged. Congress spokesman VN Gadgil said these ministers had not applied for entry.
The Observer
LEFT WILL HAVE ITS SAY IN BUDGET FRAMING

The Left parties are preparing to take on Finance Minister P. Chidambaram at the forthcoming United Front (UF) steering committee meeting, over the government's economic policy. It views the government's policies as a legacy and continuation of the previous government's economic policy. The Left is determined to press the government to withdraw the insurance regulatory bill, which seeks to open up the insurance sector to foreign participation. It will also mount pressure to get the Lok Pal (Ombudsman) and electoral reforms bills, among others, passed in the budget session.
The Economic Times
DRAFT BROADCAST BILL ALLOWS FOREIGN EQUITY

A 49 percent foreign equity limit has been proposed in the revised draft broadcast bill. Foreign equity can be brought in only in media companies incorporated in the country. Anything beyond the 49 percent limit of foreign equity would change the nature of the company to a foreign company, which would not be allowed to function from the country. The earlier draft, which was expected to have been tabled in the winter session of parliament, had stipulated a 25 percent foreign equity limit. The draft bill is now awaiting cabinet approval.
PAKISTAN SEEKS SUGAR INDUSTRY'S HELP

Pakistan sought assistance from the Indian sugar industry for the prompt sale of 50,000 tonnes of sugar as the State Trading Corporation (STC) professed its inability to deliver on schedule. The Pakistan deal is STC's first contract in the international market after the decanalisation of sugar exports. The contract is now expected to be allotted to the industry's foreign trade body - ISGEIC - instead, sources said. Pakistan, which is facing a shortage, had issued a global tender on December 12, 1996 for buying 50,000 tonnes of sugar. Meanwhile, the Commerce Ministry has convened a meeting between the STC chairman and the sugar industry for arriving at a consensus on future global bidding
TAX REFORMS ON CARDS: FINANCE MINISTER

Tax rates would be lowered in the forthcoming budget, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram indicated, while assuring there was a consensus in the government on reforms. The minister was trying to allay fears of investors, particularly foreign companies, about divergent opinions within the United Front. The finance minister said a decision on the minimum alternate tax would be announced soon. Referring to the government's divestment programme, the minister said Bharat Heavy Electricals, National Thermal Power Corporation and Steel Authority of India, the crown jewels of the Indian public sector, should be privatised for their own good. Financial Express
TATA GROUP INITIATES MAJOR RESTRUCTURING

The 300 billion rupee Tata group initiated a major restructuring exercise to transform its 80-odd companies into a tightly-knit organisation. The group appointed McKinsey and Company to work out a detailed group structure. McKinsey would look at the group's activities and submit its recommendations in a year. Company sources said the move was linked to the group's proposal of promoting the Tata brand name by charging a user fee from various companies. The Tatas also appointed the British firm Wolff Olins to work on the Tata brand proposal -- defining the brand and drawing up a group logo.
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX LEAPS 74 POINTS

Foreign institutional investors made their first major entry on 1997 on the Indian bourses, leading to a rally in stock prices. Dealers said sentiments were buoyed following the government's resolve to attract around $10 billion foreign investments every year. The Bombay Stock Exchange sensitive index closed at 3,362.39 with a net gain of 73.51 points from the previous close of 3,288.88. The 50-share National Stock Exchange gained a total of 9.90 points when it closed at 956.60 from the previous close of 946.70.
TRANSPARENCY TO BE GOVERNMENT'S TOUCHSTONE: PREMIER

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda has made it clear that middlemen would not be allowed in deals between the government and any other party. The country, he said, had suffered because of middlemen in the past and hence it was decided to do away with this practice. The government was also trying to minimise procedural delays by reducing bureaucratic approvals and simplifying norms for investment, including foreign direct investment (FDI), he said. Assuring industry of taking further steps in this direction in the next fortnight, he claimed FDI proposals worth $6.5 billion had already been cleared over the past four-five months.
STATE BANK OF INDIA GETS MANDATE FOR ICICI LOAN

The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) will raise a five-year $125 million foreign currency loan. The loan will be raised at an all-in cost of 68 basis points over six-month Libor. The mandate for the club deal was given to the State Bank of India and five Japanese banks. ICICI sources said this was the finest rate ICICI had ever got in the syndicated loan market. Its last syndicated loan was raised at 74 basis points over Libor, sources added.
GOVERNMENT URGED TO RATIFY OILFIELD AWARD TO ESSAR

British High Commissioner to India David Gore-Booth has written to the petroleum minister requesting early ratification of the award of the Ratna R series oilfield to the Essar Oil-Premier Oil combine. A government panel had recommended the field be awarded to Essar in December 1995. The combine was the front-runner for the project and was even recommended by the technical evaluation committee. However, ONGC, the owner of the field, was believed to be lobbying for developing it on its own now. Competitors had alleged serious lapses in the award and the Finance Ministry had also asked for clarifications. Given the situation, the British high commission decided to intervene on behalf of th
Business Standard
EXCHANGE CONTROL NORMS EASED

In a move to liberalise current account transactions, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) scrapped the ceiling on foreign exchange remittances overseas for 11 purposes. Earlier, monies remitted abroad above a prescribed ceiling had to be cleared by the central bank. The RBI said it did not fear capital flight on this count. Sources said the relaxation was expected to increase the remittances by 5-10 percent. The RBI went ahead with the move after it found the outflow due to relaxation in the foreign exchange travel quotas was marginal.
GLOBAL FLOTATION OF GOVERNMENT DEBT TO FORM PART OF BUDGET

The government is slated to include its maiden international sovereign borrowing in the budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March). The move is aimed at ensuring transparency and parliamentary approval for the entire transaction. The government is considering a flotation of around $200-300 million. However, with the modalites still being worked out, it is not clear whether this would also pave the way for the participation of foreign institutional investors in the government securities market.
INDUSTRIAL GROWTH HIT BY FALL IN CRUDE OUTPUT

A 10 percent negative growth in crude production in the first eight months of the current fiscal year contributed substantially to slack industrial growth in recent months, the industry minister said. The minister said refinery products continued to witness buoyancy and recorded a growth of 6.3 percent in the current financial year. Latest data indicated industrial production improved by 9.8 percent this fiscal from 8.5 percent in April-August, 1996. The industry minister said consumption of petroleum products increased from 55 million tonnes in 1990/91 (April-March) to 69 million tonnes in the previous year. Demand was expected to go up to 124 million tonnes in the next 12 years. Almost
GOVERNMENT PLANS RAPID FISCAL CORRECTION OVER TWO YEARS

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said he was planning a rapid fiscal correction over the next two years to check the ballooning fiscal deficit of 624 billion rupees. He said the correction would have to be effected through additional revenues, more than through a reduction in government expenditure. Chidambaram said the correction would be sought to be achieved through a sensible tax policy, but made it clear that a reduction in tax rates could only be made in proportion to the widening of the tax base. The finance minister called for examining methods to bring more people in the tax net by reducing the rates and simplifying the procedure.
TELECOM LICENCES ASSIGNABLE ONLY TO RECOGNISED DONERS

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has decided to make basic telecommunication services licences assignable only to recognised domestic financial institutions. The DoT decision is said to have upset the companies which hold letters of intent to provide the services. Lenders, including domestic and foreign institutions and banks, have been asking for assignability of telecommunication licences since the value of the operating companies' assets is not enough to cover the huge loan requirements envisaged in the sector.
REFORMS PACKAGE FOR INDUSTRY BY MONTH-END

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda admitted that measures for simplifying investment procedures and hasten industrial growth would be delayed. Although the government had promised to unveil reforms by January 15, 1997, the prime minister said the measures would be announced early February. A meeting with industry and trade chiefs at the end of 1996 had already turned around the two-month decline in the capital market, he added. The areas identified for action in the meeting included full convertibility of the rupee, cutting interest rates and helping domestic companies compete with foreign rivals. He also confirmed that some key infrastructure areas had been identified for private sector par
The Observer
TELECOM DEPARTMENT CLEARS FACILITY FOR CELLULAR OPERATORS

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has agreed to allow cellular operators to use private basic operators' network for transmitting intra-circle calls. However, for transmitting inter-circle and international calls, cellular operators have to connect to the DoT network. The operators have, for the time being, agreed to the decision. However, basic operators are gearing up to pressurise the DoT to refer the issue to the Telecom Regulatory Authority within two years for a review, sources said.
BEST & CROMPTON MAY FALL IN INDONESIAN FIRM'S LAP

Indonesian multinational Polisindo is likely to take over Best & Crompton, an ailing Vijay Mallya company. With interests in textiles, light engineering, polyester chemicals, Polisindo plans to enter the power sector in India. It is keen on Best & Crompton because of synergies in handing out likely contracts to its engineering wing. The group has already contacted banks, institutions and promoters expressing its desire for a takeover. It had also conducted a feasibility study for the company by Coopers and Lybrand, and a concrete proposal is likely this month. Polisindo plans to bring in funds by March this year.
MORE INCENTIVES FOR FOREIGN INVESTMENT: PREMIER

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said his government was poised to take significant decisions to improve the climate for foreign investment, regardless of opposition from certain quarters. He said his government was determined to attract $10 billion in foreign investment annually and promised steps to attract foreign investment, before his departure for the World Economic Summit in Davos later this month.
